ON THE 8 th OF SEPTEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 5521 of 2019  SATYANARAYAN  Versus  BAJAJ ALLIANCE INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Abhishek Gilke, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Monesh Jindal, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER
The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 30.7.2019 passed in Claim Case No.5/2018.
The Insurance Company has filed its cross-objections on the question of quantum of compensation by disputing the loss of earning capacity at 10% as concluded by the claims Tribunal.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 28.1.2016 appellant was going by his motorcycle No.MP-42-MJ-3598 from Ujjain to his village.

When he reached near Tajpur Choupati at around 5.00 in the evening, respondent No.2 came driving Swift D'zire Car No.MP-09-CP-8381 from the side of Maksi in rash and negligent manner and dashed into motorcycle of the appellant, because of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He sustained fractures in femur bone of his right leg, tibia fibula bone, calcaneum bone, callus bone as well as metatarsal bone.
2.1 The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the appellant.

The claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25461 2 MA-5521-2019 Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,72,320/-, out of which an amount of Rs.1,56,447/- was for expenditure incurred in treatment for the injuries.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims Tribunal has not correctly assessed the expenditure.

He points out that he had to incur a total expenditure of Rs.2,26,880/- in treatment,
while the claims Tribunal has awarded only Rs.1,56,447/-.
He further submits that though the claims Tribunal considered Ex.P/131 to P/157, which were receipts of the travel had to done by the appellant for getting treated at Ujjain.

However, no amount has been awarded by the claims Satyanarayan vs Bajaj Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88467735/
1 Tribunal for such travel expenses.

sentences.text: He further points out that he remained under treatment for a long period of 11 months.
However, the claims Tribunal has not awarded anything for the period for which he remained out of job.
4. Per contra , learned counsel for the respondent No1/Insurance Company submits that proper amount of compensation has been awarded for medical expenses and no interference is warranted in the same.
Apart from this, he points out that the claims Tribunal in para 30 and 31 of the impugned award has considered permanent disability of the appellant.
He was posted as Sales Officer in the HDFC Bank before the accident and he had resigned before the accident.
Thus, there was no loss of earning to the appellant during the period of treatment and also there is no loss of earning due to permanent disability sustained by the appellant.
Thus, the claims Tribunal has erred in treating it at 10%.

He submits that according to the cause title of the appeal appellant is still working as Sales Officer in HDFC Bank and he has not demonstrated by leading evidence that his salary has been affected by the accident.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25461 3 MA-5521-2019 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. From the document Ex.P/7 to P/21 and bills Ex.P/131 to P/132 it is clear that appellant has incurred expenditure of Rs.2,26,880/- in his treatment due to accident, while the claims Tribunal has awarded only an amount of Rs.1,56,447/-.
Thus, an additional amount of Rs.70,443/- is awarded to the appellant for expenditure in his treatment due to accident.
As regards the charges of transportation on a bare perusal of Ex.P/131 to P/157 it can be seen that the same are handwritten receipts without any dispatch or registration of the taxi owner.
The claims Tribunal in para 37 of the award has clearly recorded that the alleged taxi is a private vehicle.
The appellant is not able to displace such findings of the claims Tribunal.

In this view of the matter the amount of Rs.10,000/-
as awarded by the claims Tribunal for transportation is held to be correct.

7. As regards loss of earning during treatment it is seen from the evidence of the appellant that he stated in para 18 of his cross-examination he admitted that he had resigned on 22.1.2016 from the HDFC Bank.
As such, before the date of accident i.e. 28.1.2016 he himself has resigned.
The appellant has not demonstrated by leading any evidence that the accident caused loss of income in view of the fact of resignation is on record.
As such for loss of earning during the period of treatment is also not to be awarded.

8. As regards contention of the Insurance Company that permanent disability at 10% has been assessed by the claims Tribunal on a very higher side and without any evidence available for the same, it can be seen from findings recorded by the claims Tribunal in para 31 that the appellant has suffered 40% permanent disability for which Ex.P/189 permanent disability certificate was issued and the permanent disability was proved by Dr. H.S.Rana, who was examined as PW-4.

The certificate was issued by the District Medical Board, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25461 4 MA-5521-2019 Ujjain.

sentences.text:
From the evidence of the appellant it has come on record in para 23 that because of his accident he could not join Trushna Finance Service, he was Satyanarayan vs Bajaj Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88467735/
2 offered employment by the said concern.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there is no doubt that the earning of the appellant was affected by the accident.
The claims Tribunal has also recorded that the appellant has suffered 40% permanent disability in his right leg.
Thus, considering the same at 10% for overall body does not appear to be very high.
In this view of the matter the cross-objections filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.

9. In view of the above analysis the appeal is partly allowed to the extent that Insurance Company is directed to pay further amount of Rs.70,433/- to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing claim application till its payment.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Satyanarayan vs Bajaj Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88467735/
